name: Muddy Brown
lede: Muddy Brown is a dull, yellow-leaning brown from a 2010 crowd color survey, a dirtier-looking neighbor of Milk Chocolate and Mustard on screen.

sections.title: A descriptive compound
sections.body:
The library's only source for Muddy Brown is the xkcd 2010 survey; no dictionary or paint brand in our data uses the phrase, so its coining is undocumented beyond that [1]. At hex #886806 it measures lightness 46 and chroma 52 in LCH, a fairly dark, muted brown-yellow [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by CIEDE2000 are [[bistre-brown|Bistre Brown]], 4.2 units off and read as lighter, and [[antique|Antique]], 4.3 units off and duller [2]. The nearest gem comparison is deep "Madeira" [[gem:citrine|citrine]], 5.7 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this brown in 340 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.43%, as photographed, more common than 68% of the named colors here [4]. The earliest match is a 1375 painting, 635 years before the name's own 2010 record, which only shows an aged, varnished canvas can resemble this hue, not that anyone mixed this exact paint then, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. Paulus Potter is its most devoted painter, present in 4 of his 28 works, 8.9 times the baseline rate [4]. It shares canvases with [[mud|Mud Green]] and [[fallen-leaf|Fallen leaf]] more than chance would predict, and inside a painting it most often plays an accent [4].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a descriptive compound of muddy + brown
